A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaptiveStep and ASPRM. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched, including retained appendix figures that are renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASPRM evaluations on mathematical reasoning and code generation, including BoN, token-level value-guided decoding, generalization experiments, and training-data analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a threshold sensitivity study and an analysis relating training-question accuracy to division counts.

M1.justification: Equation (3) corrects the reported PRM training objective by adding a minus sign to the log-likelihood sum. Confidence-based division, rollout labeling, and TVD remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or retraining associated with this correction.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same mathematical reasoning and code-generation coverage, including GSM8k, MATH/MATH500, GSM-Symbolic, LeetCodeDataset, and LiveCodeBench. The new analyses use existing GSM8k coverage; additional generator sizes are model configurations, not new tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Math-Shepherd, ER-PRM, and the code ORM remain the evaluated comparison methods in the corresponding existing experiments. The new threshold study reuses Math-Shepherd and ER-PRM as backbone-matched baselines without introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds GSM8k Bo64 evaluations at division thresholds of 0.5%, 1%, and 1.5% alongside the existing 2% setting, using MetaMATH-Llama-7b, -13b, and -70b candidate generators. These are additional experimental configurations; the original benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two focused analyses: Section 4.4/Figure 6 tests sensitivity to the division threshold across PRM backbones and generator sizes, while Appendix A.4/Figure 9 examines whether difficult training questions receive few divisions. Existing transferability, generalization, mixed-data, feature, and case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Figure 9 adds a regression line, 70th/80th/90th percentile reference lines, and a 'Rollout 64 Train Dataset' label for the training-data diagnostic. These add statistical summaries and sampling information, without establishing increased repetitions or new uncertainty reporting for the existing benchmark results.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds threshold-dependent GSM8k Bo64 results, and Appendix A.4 reports a 1.62% low-accuracy, low-division subset. These are new findings under additional analysis settings. Tables 1–12 and the corresponding original benchmark and dataset-statistics figures retain their results.

T1.justification: Equation (3) receives a mathematical correction: a leading minus sign and explicit grouping of the binary cross-entropy terms. The other method equations and definitions remain unchanged, and neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions: automatic confidence-based step division, strong BoN performance, TVD improvements over greedy decoding, reduced construction costs, and applicability to mathematics and code. The abstract rewrite does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the original 2% choice by explaining that optimal thresholds depend on model capability and interpreting stronger models as needing less training data. It also explains the rollout-cost restriction on the sweep and discusses difficult questions with few divisions as an uncommon condition in the analyzed training data.

D1.justification: v2 documents threshold values, generator sizes, and PRM/baseline pairings for the new sensitivity experiment, plus limited rollout information for Figure 9. Existing implementation and resource disclosures remain essentially unchanged; the printed GitHub address identifies the same repository already linked in v1.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage and research positioning are retained. Publication metadata updates for Chaffin and Chen, consolidation of duplicate Ma references, and shortened author lists do not add or remove distinct cited works.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, makes scattered language corrections, updates affiliations and acknowledgments, and inserts Section 4.4 and Appendix A.4. The main narrative remains intact, with Feature Analysis renumbered and the acknowledgment/impact-statement ordering adjusted.

P2.justification: v2 adds the threshold plots in Figure 6 and the training-distribution plot in Figure 9. Existing appendix Figures 6–7 become Figures 7–8, with the candidate-statistics figure repositioned to accommodate the new plot. Introductory diagrams and page layout also receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the loss formula and provides empirical checks of the previously fixed 2% threshold and the possibility of difficult questions receiving few divisions. These additions improve correctness and support for the method while preserving the original benchmark evidence. The gains remain limited because the new analyses concern GSM8k and a restricted threshold range.
